# cpanel_api_token (Resource)

Manages a full-access cPanel API token and its optional expiration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cpanel_api_token" "automation" {
  name = "terraform-automation"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The API token name. Renaming updates a non-active token without rotating its secret.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (Number) The future Unix timestamp when the token expires, or `0` for no expiration. Changing it rotates the token.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) The token creation time as a Unix timestamp.
- `features` (Set of String) The feature names attached to a limited token imported from cPanel. Newly created tokens have full access.
- `has_full_access` (Boolean) Whether cPanel reports that the token has full account access.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The API token secret. cPanel returns it only during creation, so imported resources cannot recover it.
- `whitelist_ips` (Set of String) The source IP restrictions reported by cPanel.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cpanel_api_token.automation terraform-automation
```
